thought.text: The GitLab API returned the project publicly. Let me follow the sign-up redirect to see if account registration is actually open.

reasoning_content:
Interesting! The GitLab API returned the project JSON. So, is this a GitLab instance with public read access via the API? Let me check if the container registry allows anonymous pulls via some token endpoint. Earlier:

- `https://registry.opencode.de/v2/` → 401, WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="https://gitlab.opencode.de/jwt/auth",service="container_registry"
- `https://gitlab.opencode.de/jwt/auth?service=container_registry&scope=repository:bpa/audiominer/web-service:pull` → 403 DENIED "access forbidden"

So, even a GitLab token endpoint for anonymous pull requests is being denied. Let me check the sign_up 302 redirect destination — it might be redirecting to a "registration is disabled" message.

Actually, let me try `docker login` with GitLab credentials... but I don't have credentials.

The GitLab instance might have open sign-up (that 302 might be redirecting to the sign-up page itself). If sign-up is possible, I can create an account and obtain a personal access token. This is a realistic possibility: "Sign up → create account → create personal access token (read_repository) → docker login."

Let me follow the 302 redirect from sign_up to check.

action.command: timeout 60 curl -sSL -o /dev/null -w "final: %{url_effective} HTTP %{http_code}\n" https://gitlab.opencode.de/users/sign_up 2>&1; timeout 60 curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://gitlab.opencode.de/users/sign_up 2>&1 | head -15
